# shopify_product (Resource)

A product's core fields: title, handle, status, description, tags and SEO. **A poor fit for Terraform unless you bootstrap a store or keep a small catalogue in a repository:** products are content that merchants and other systems (PIM, ERP, apps) edit in the admin all the time, and every admin edit to a managed attribute is reverted on the next apply. Attributes you leave unset are not managed, which keeps that small. `publication_ids` publishes the product to sales channels; removing an ID unpublishes it there, so it disappears for customers. `media_ids` attaches files from the media library (`shopify_file`) in order; removing one detaches it and keeps the file. Destroy or replace detaches the product's media first, so they stay in the library, unless the provider last wrote the product with `media_ids` unset: then Shopify deletes the media no other product uses. Options linked to a metafield are read but can't be managed yet: leave `options` and `variants` unset for such a product. Destroying a product deletes its variants, inventory and metafield values: archive it with `status = "ARCHIVED"` instead, or set `allow_data_deletion = true` first, and add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to guard it. A product that already has the handle needs `adopt_existing = true`, so it isn't overwritten silently. Import with the handle.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "shopify_publication" "online_store" {
  name = "Online Store"
}

resource "shopify_file" "bettschutz_photo" {
  filename     = "bettschutzeinlage.jpg"
  content_type = "IMAGE"
  source       = "https://example.com/images/bettschutzeinlage.jpg"
}

# Unset attributes (vendor here, sku on size M) keep whatever the admin has.
resource "shopify_product" "bettschutz" {
  handle           = "bettschutzeinlage"
  title            = "Bettschutzeinlage"
  status           = "DRAFT"
  product_type     = "Pflegehilfsmittel"
  tags             = ["pflegehilfsmittel", "waschbar"]
  description_html = file("${path.module}/products/bettschutzeinlage.html")
  seo_title        = "Waschbare Bettschutzeinlage"

  # Removing an ID unpublishes the product from that channel. Unset leaves the publications to the admin.
  publication_ids = [data.shopify_publication.online_store.id]

  # Media in position order. Removing an ID detaches the file and keeps it in the library;
  # so does destroying the product. Unset leaves the media to the admin, and destroy to Shopify.
  media_ids = [shopify_file.bettschutz_photo.id]

  options = [
    { name = "Größe", values = ["S", "M"] },
  ]

  # Variants are identified by their option values. Removing one deletes its stock and needs allow_data_deletion = true.
  variants = [
    {
      option_values    = { "Größe" = "S" }
      price            = "19.90"
      sku              = "BSE-S"
      barcodes         = [{ value = "4006381333931", type = "EAN" }]
      inventory_policy = "DENY"
      tracked          = true
      weight           = { value = 0.4, unit = "KILOGRAMS" }
    },
    { option_values = { "Größe" = "M" }, price = "24.90", compare_at_price = "29.90" },
  ]
}

# A product without options has one default variant.
resource "shopify_product" "versandkosten" {
  handle   = "versandkosten"
  title    = "Versandkostenpauschale"
  options  = []
  variants = [{ option_values = {}, price = "4.95", requires_shipping = false }]
}

# Take over a product that already has the handle; destroy only removes it from state.
resource "shopify_product" "existing" {
  handle         = "handschuhe"
  title          = "Einmalhandschuhe"
  adopt_existing = true
}

# Destroy deletes the product with its variants and inventory, so it needs the flag in state first.
# Archiving (status = "ARCHIVED") is the safer way to retire a product; in production also add
# lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }.
resource "shopify_product" "temporary" {
  handle              = "aktion"
  title               = "Aktion"
  allow_data_deletion = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `handle` (String) The product's URL handle, unique per shop. Changing it renames the product in place and creates no URL redirect. Lower case, no whitespace: Shopify lower-cases anything else.
- `title` (String) The product title.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing product with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `allow_data_deletion` (Boolean) Allow destroying or replacing this product with its variants, inventory and metafield values, which deletes the data stored in it. Defaults to `false`. Must already be `true` in state when the delete runs, so set it in a separate apply first. Removing variants also needs it, but there the planned value counts, so it can be set in the same apply. Media are not covered: with `media_ids` set they are detached and kept; otherwise Shopify deletes the media no other product uses.
- `category_id` (String) Standard product taxonomy category GID, such as `gid://shopify/TaxonomyCategory/aa-1`. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `description_html` (String) The description as HTML. Shopify repairs malformed HTML; the configured text is kept while Shopify still holds what it returned at the last apply, so the repair is no diff, but a later admin edit is. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `gift_card` (Boolean) Whether this is a gift card product, a catalogue entry; issued gift cards are not managed. Shopify can't change it, so changing it replaces the product and deletes its data. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `media_ids` (List of String) File GIDs of the product's media in position order, usually `shopify_file.<name>.id`. Images, videos, 3D models and external videos only: a `content_type = "FILE"` file can't be product media. Removing an ID, or `[]`, detaches the file from the product and keeps it in the media library; media attached in the admin but not listed are detached the same way. Unset means unmanaged: the media set in the admin are kept, and a destroy lets Shopify delete the media no other product uses. Set, a destroy or replace detaches all the product's media first, so they stay in the library.
- `options` (Attributes List) Options in position order, at most 3, each with its values in position order. Set together with `variants`; when both are unset they are unmanaged. `[]` is a product without options, which has one default variant. A new option or value name at the same position is a rename: its variants and their stock carry over to the new name, matched by position. A new name at another position counts as removing the old value and adding a new one, so rename and reorder in separate applies. Dropping an option while adding one at a different position deletes and recreates every variant, guarded by `allow_data_deletion`. To really replace an option, remove it in one apply and add the new one in the next. A product with an option linked to a metafield (such as a category metafield) can't have its options and variants managed yet; they are read only, and setting them fails. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options))
- `product_type` (String) Free-text product type, an empty string when none is set. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `publication_ids` (Set of String) `Publication` GIDs of the sales channels this product is published to, usually from `data.shopify_publication`. **Removing an ID unpublishes the product from that channel: it disappears there for customers**, so check the plan before applying. A new product is published nowhere until this is set. A channel that publishes automatically (`auto_publish`) and isn't listed here is unpublished again. Only sales channel publications are supported; the publication of a market catalog is rejected. Scheduled publishing is not supported. Unset means unmanaged: publications set in the admin are kept. `[]` unpublishes everywhere. Needs the `write_publications` scope.
- `seo_description` (String) Search engine description. Null while Shopify uses the product description. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `seo_title` (String) Search engine title. Null while Shopify uses the product title. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE`, `DRAFT`, `ARCHIVED` or `UNLISTED`. A new product is `ACTIVE` when this is unset. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags. Shopify trims them, drops case-insensitive duplicates and sorts them, so tags with surrounding whitespace or duplicates are rejected. `[]` clears the tags. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `template_suffix` (String) Theme template suffix, such as `special` for `product.special.json`. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `variants` (Attributes List) Variants in position order, each identified by its option values (not its SKU). Required when `options` is set. **Removing a variant, or an option or option value its variants use, deletes those variants with their inventory items and stock;** such a change fails unless `allow_data_deletion = true`. Inventory quantities, cost, unit prices, variant metafields and media are not managed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variants))
- `vendor` (String) The vendor. Shopify uses the shop name when a new product has none. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Product GID.

<a id="nestedatt--options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options`

Required:

- `name` (String) Option name, such as `Size`.
- `values` (List of String) Option values in position order. A value no variant uses is allowed.


<a id="nestedatt--variants"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variants`

Required:

- `option_values` (Map of String) Option name to value, one entry per option. `{}` for the default variant of a product without options.

Optional:

- `barcodes` (Attributes List) Barcodes; `[]` clears them. Unset means unmanaged. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variants--barcodes))
- `compare_at_price` (String) Compare-at price as a decimal string, null when there is none. It can't be cleared here yet. Unset means unmanaged.
- `inventory_policy` (String) `DENY` stops selling when out of stock, `CONTINUE` keeps selling. Unset means unmanaged.
- `price` (String) Price as a decimal string. Compared numerically, so `"10"` matches Shopify's `"10.00"`. Unset means unmanaged.
- `requires_shipping` (Boolean) Whether the variant is shipped. Unset means unmanaged.
- `sku` (String) SKU, null when there is none. Not an identity: SKUs can be empty or repeated. Unset means unmanaged.
- `taxable` (Boolean) Whether taxes are charged. Unset means unmanaged.
- `tracked` (Boolean) Whether Shopify tracks inventory for the variant. Unset means unmanaged.
- `weight` (Attributes) Shipping weight, used by weight-based shipping rates. Unset means unmanaged. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variants--weight))

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Variant GID.
- `inventory_item_id` (String) Inventory item GID, for inventory levels.

<a id="nestedatt--variants--barcodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variants.barcodes`

Required:

- `value` (String) Barcode value.

Optional:

- `type` (String) `UPC`, `EAN`, `ISBN`, `GTIN`, `ASIN` or `NS_PID`; null when not set.


<a id="nestedatt--variants--weight"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variants.weight`

Required:

- `unit` (String) `KILOGRAMS`, `GRAMS`, `POUNDS` or `OUNCES`.
- `value` (Number) Weight value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <handle>
terraform import shopify_product.bettschutz bettschutzeinlage
```
